title: Residual load and the power price
question: Does the hourly day-ahead price rise with residual load, and more clearly than with load?

issues.text: Hours next to each other are strongly autocorrelated; 1,464 hours are far fewer independent observations.
issues.fix: Read the interval as optimistic; repeat with daily means (61 days) or another two months.

issues.text: Residual load and price both follow the clock and the weather.
issues.fix: The mechanism (merit order) is known; the test asks whether the data shows it, and the stack chart shows which plants move with it.

alternatives.question: Is the curve steeper above 35 GW residual load than below 20 GW?
alternatives.why: Drill down: the convexity of the supply curve (segments step).

alternatives.question: Does the whole curve move up with the gas price from month to month?
alternatives.why: Expand: needs TTF gas and EU ETS prices.

hypotheses.statement: The hourly day-ahead price increases with residual load.
hypotheses.null: The price does not change with residual load.

hypotheses.statement: At the hourly grain the price falls as wind and solar output rises.
hypotheses.null: The price does not change with wind + solar output.

concepts.label: Day-ahead electricity price
concepts.description: Hourly mean DE-LU day-ahead price, EUR/MWh.

concepts.label: Residual load
concepts.description: Load minus wind and solar, GW.
concepts.why: The predictor the merit order names.

concepts.label: Variable renewables
concepts.description: Wind (on- and offshore) plus solar, GW.
concepts.why: The part of supply with near-zero marginal cost.

concepts.label: Gas price
concepts.why: Shifts the steep end of the curve; a confounder across months.

strategy.detail: A daily gas price series (e.g. ENTSOG or a commodity API), joined on the day.

data.request: Daily TTF gas price for May–June 2026
data.source: ICE Endex Dutch TTF settlement prices (not in the Explore catalog, no keyless API known: fetch by hand)
data.why: To separate the curve's shift from its shape.

method.summary: Regress the hourly price on residual load (H1) and on wind+solar (H2); the fit step gives the least-squares slope and R² for load, residual load and wind+solar side by side.

steps.title: Join on the quarter-hour
steps.detail: quarters step: one row per unix second of the quarter-hour, then hourly means.

steps.title: Fit price on each predictor
steps.detail: fit step: slope_eur_per_gwh, r2 for residual load, load, wind + solar.

steps.title: Check the shape
steps.detail: segments step: slope below 20 GW, 20–35 GW and above 35 GW.

steps.title: Accept or reject H1 and H2
steps.detail: Then repeat for a winter month and another bidding zone.

caveats: Hours are autocorrelated: the effective sample is much smaller than 1,464.
Two months of one season; gas and CO₂ prices move the curve between seasons.
Linear fits on a convex curve understate the slope at high residual load.
Day-ahead prices only; intraday and balancing prices react to forecast errors.
